title: All-HiFloat8 PFA: four publication bodies and five precision studies
formula: out(B*MQ,128) bf16 = sum_n hif8(exp(s - m)) @ V / sum(exp(s - m)), s = Q K^T / sqrt(128) over uint8 HiFloat8 Q(B*MQ,128) and K/V(B*N,128); nz and v8 bias the exponent by ln16 so P and its denominator both carry a factor of 16, while v9 and study_v2/study_v4 hold s and the online state in FP16
study_for: The variant list is the lesson index. `nd` publishes P key-major in ND; `nz` builds NZ directly in UB with a four-key deinterleave at physical stride 33; `v8` groups three physical 128-key score tiles under one maximum update so three P beats accumulate into a single L0C PV result; `v9` exports the score to FP16 through two SINGLE drains with a FixP19 scale. Four answers to "how does P get from the vector side back to the cube".

The five `study_*` bodies are the other axis: ONE schedule held fixed while two things move. V1/V2 take the FixP19 scale at the fixpipe drain and V3/V4 take it in the vector function; V1/V3 keep FP32 state and V2/V4 keep FP16. The fifth, `study_v3_splitn`, moves neither -- it is V3's arithmetic through a single SPLITN fixpipe bridge instead of two SINGLE ones, which is why it needs scale 1.0 (SPLITN cannot requantize). All five are complete attention kernels with their own cases; the thing that is not a kernel is the `_nocv` companion each of them has, whose cube-to-vector mutexes are replaced by a no-op so a missing handoff shows up as a wrong value rather than a hang.

`v8`'s credit ring holds six ordered P0/P1/P2 beats, and `v9` retires exactly three beats for every final-group length from 1 to 384 -- including a phase-only P2 that uses the same event pair as a real one. That is how a variable-length tail keeps a fixed-shape pipeline honest, and the nine `v9_*` boundary cases (N = 1, 127, 128, 129, 255, 256, 257, 383, 897) are the enumeration of it.
do_not_copy_when: You are picking a winner from the archived campaigns. The HQ8/S4099 and HQ40/S9360 numbers quoted in the v8 and v9 module headers are source history and select nothing; nothing here is a speed claim.
You need the `nocv` bodies to be correct. They are diagnostics whose synchronisation is removed on purpose, no case runs them, and running one and getting a number proves nothing.

Your last key group can be shorter than 129 keys and you are copying `v8`. Its source domain is 129..384 keys in the final group, because a zero second tile does not retire its event beat. `v9` is the variant that handles every positive tail, and this demo no longer has the host-side guard that used to reject the short case before launching it.
